title: Shortest Stretch With Enough Total
statement:
Find the **shortest non-empty contiguous stretch** of `numbers` whose sum is **at least `target`**, and return its length, or `-1` if no stretch is large enough.

The numbers can be **negative**, which makes a stretch longer sometimes make the sum smaller. (When all numbers are positive a plain sliding window is enough; here it is not.)

examples.explanation: The stretch 4, -2, 6 adds up to 8. No stretch of length 1 or 2 reaches 8.
Even the whole list adds up to only 3.

hints.nudge: Write the sum of any stretch as a difference of two prefix sums. Which earlier prefix sums can you throw away because they can never give a shorter stretch?
hints.pattern: Prefix sums plus a monotonic deque: keep candidate start positions with increasing prefix sums; pop from the front while the stretch is long enough, pop from the back while a later start is at least as good.
hints.pseudocode:
prefix[0] = 0, prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + numbers[i]
window = empty deque of positions
for j in 0..n:
  while window not empty and prefix[j] - prefix[front] >= target: best = min(best, j - front); pop front
  while window not empty and prefix[back] >= prefix[j]: pop back
  push j at the back
return best or -1
hints.walkthrough: A stretch from position i to j (j after i) has the sum prefix[j] - prefix[i]. For every j we want the LATEST i with prefix[i] <= prefix[j] - target. A plain two-pointer window fails because with negative numbers the sum is not monotonic. Keep a deque of candidate starts i whose prefix sums are increasing. Two rules: (1) if the front start already gives a sum >= target for the current j, record the length and remove it: any later j would only give a longer stretch for it. (2) before adding j as a candidate, remove from the back every start with a prefix sum >= prefix[j], because j is later AND not larger, so it is always at least as good. Every position enters and leaves the deque once: O(n).
